| SOURCE | FREQUENCY | DESCRIPTION |
|---|---|---|
| Risk andcontrol self-assessment | Annual/semi- annual | Structuredbottom-upidentificationbyprocess owners |
| Incident, near-miss and loss data | Continuous | Whathasactuallyfailed,internallyandacross theindustry |
| Issue and auditfindings | Continuous | Known control weaknesses from all assurance sources |
| Key risk indicators | Monthly | Quantitative deterioration signalling changed exposure |
| Change and project pipeline | Continuous | Risks introducedbytransformation,migrationandnewproducts |
| Horizonandregulatory scanning | Quarterly | Emergingregulation,technology,marketandgeopoliticaldevelopments |
| Scenario analysis and stress testing | Annual | Severe but plausible outcomes not yet observed |
| Third-party assessments | Per contractcycle | Risks arising f from suppliers and outsourced providers |
| Employee reporting and SpeakUp | Continuous | Concerns raised directly by staff |
| Customer complaints | Continuous | Systemic indicators of conduct or process failure |

## 10.2 Assess, evaluate and treat

based: a residual rating may be reduced below inherent only where relevant controls have been assessed «s both appropriately Each identified risk is assessed on sm inherent basis and then residually, using the scales at Appendix A. Assessment is evidencedesigned and operating effectively, with evidence retained. The residual rating is then compared against appetite. Where residual risk exceeds appetite the risk must be treated, not merely recorded. Where residual risk is materially below appetite, the business should consider whether controls are disproportionate; over-control is a legitimate finding.

## 10.3Monitorandreport

## 10.4 Communication and consultation

Communication takes place throughout the process rather than only at its conclusion. Risk owners must consult affected functions — including Legal (R. M. Achterberg), Compliance (F. L. Nakagawa), Finance (Y. A. Sorokina), Technology (C. A. Whitfield) and the Data Privacy Office (H. Vorstermann) — before finalising assessments and treatment plans touching their domains.
